messages:
Maria K: Heads-up — after the quickrollout this morning (20% canary -> 100%) some tenants reported weird aggregated metrics in Console. Looks like charts are showing combined request counts across orgs for certain routes.
Ryan H: ugh. any reproducer? which routes?
Maria K: noticed on /console/insights and internal metrics dashboards. Telemetry shows spikes that don't match logs. Example: org A shows +12k tokens at 09:02 but our access logs only have ~200 reqs for org A at that time.
Jess L: do we have a prefetch/kv-cache key that could be getting shared?
Maria K: that's my suspicion. The quickrollout changed the routing policy to use affinity header fallback: if X-ORG-AFFINITY missing -> bucket by cookie -> then fallback to global. I think ambiguous header ordering + request batching caused some hits to be attributed to the wrong shard.
InfraBot: Deploy 1719998200 by @Leo C completed: rollout quickrollout-routing-v2 to 20% at 08:55, promoted to 100% at 09:00.
Sam P: I saw the deploy, I also saw a bunch of long-lived batch requests around 09:01-09:03. Could KV cache TTL+batching hold a stale org id?
Olivia W: hmm the router code sets org from header OR cookie; there is a small race where headers are read after cookie parsing in the sidecar. If header present but empty string we treat as "unspecified" and fall back to global cluster.
Ryan H: can you paste the snippet?
Maria K: sure:
```
// router selection (simplified)
org = req.headers['x-org-affinity'] || req.cookies['org_pref'] || null
if (!org) {
  shard = globalPool.pick(req.route)
} else {
  shard = tenantPool[org].pick(req.route)
}
```

Leo C: That looks fine but the problem is some requests arrive as multipart where header gets sanitized by the proxy (empty string) and cookie parser returns previous cookie from persistent batch connection. So net effect: org becomes null while cookie contains someone else's org -> pick from tenantPool using that cookie.
Jess L: so telemetry path used header-derived org, but routing used cookie-derived org? mismatch between attribution point and routing point. That would explain metrics showing combined counts.
Sam P: Yeah, we have two different places reading org. One for routing, one for telemetry aggregation. If they disagree, telemetry aggregates into whichever one wins.
Olivia W: immediate mitigation: rollback rollout to previous routing-v1 or force header precedence+validation (treat empty string as missing and prefer cookie only if header absent).
Ryan H: can we hotfix to normalize header: `if (header === "" ) delete header` before any selection? Small change and canary quick.
Maria K: I'm running a quick heatmap compare. If we rollback, we should also run a replay to re-run attribution for the affected window (09:00-09:05) so dashboards reflect correct numbers.
InfraBot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-489 (ambiguous-routing-telemetry) by Maria K.
Leo C: I'll push a patch to treat empty header as undefined and add unit test for multipart parsing. Rolling back now as well — kicking off deploy to 0% canary.
Sam P: also add a telemetry-side guard: tag telemetry events with both header-derived and cookie-derived org, so we can reconcile quickly if mismatch happens. Short-term we can choose authoritative source for aggregation.
Jess L: oof, lesson: rollout that tweaks routing affinity needs co-ordinated change to telemetry and routing selection code. Add a checklist item to rollout playbook.
Olivia W: Agreed. I'll open a PR for playbook + the header normalization change, and a follow-up patch to backfill telemetry for the 5m window.
Maria K: thanks all — monitoring the rollback and will post updates. :thumbsup:
Leo C: rollback complete, canary -> 0%, baseline restored. I'll attach the patch and the test.
Maria K: closing loop: once PR merged, let's run reconciliation job and we can close the incident.
